blocks.text: 1. Faster R-CNN

blocks.alt: An input image goes through a shared backbone, region proposal network, then classify and regress

blocks.text: Fast R-CNN, the previous topic, still relied on a separate, slower region proposal algorithm. Faster R-CNN directly addresses that exact remaining bottleneck, explored throughout this topic.
It replaces the separate region proposal algorithm with a learned network of its own, a genuinely elegant, fully integrated solution covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Remaining Bottleneck

This connects back to a remaining bottleneck, already covered in Fast R-CNN. Fast R-CNN genuinely still relied on a separate, slower, non-learned region proposal algorithm, already covered as that topic's own final limitation.
Faster R-CNN genuinely replaces that entirely with a learned component, directly closing the exact gap already identified at the end of the previous topic.
3. The Region Proposal Network

blocks.alt: A feature map feeds the region proposal network to produce region proposals

blocks.text: Faster R-CNN's genuinely key new component connects back to shared feature computation, already covered in Fast R-CNN. The Region Proposal Network genuinely generates region proposals directly from the same shared feature map.
This directly reuses the shared computation already covered there, rather than relying on a genuinely separate, external algorithm the way both R-CNN and Fast R-CNN, already covered, still did.

blocks.text: 4. A Fully Integrated Pipeline

blocks.alt: A backbone feeds the RPN and then the ROI head in one integrated pipeline

blocks.text: This connects back to Fast R-CNN's own single forward pass, already covered. Region proposals, classification, and box regression genuinely all happen within one single, unified network now.

No genuinely separate, external algorithm is needed at all anymore, already covered as the gap this topic closes, completing the transition toward a genuinely fully learned, end-to-end Object Detection system.
5. The Anchor Box Concept

blocks.alt: Each feature map location has multiple anchor boxes

blocks.text: This connects back to the bounding box concept, already covered in Object Detection. The Region Proposal Network genuinely uses predefined anchor boxes of several different sizes and shapes as starting points.

It adjusts each anchor genuinely slightly to better match a potential object nearby, a genuinely practical technique that gives the network a genuinely reasonable starting point rather than proposing regions from complete scratch.

blocks.text: 6. The Benefit Of A Shared Backbone

blocks.alt: Fast R-CNN uses external proposals while Faster R-CNN shares the backbone

blocks.text: This connects back to Feature Maps, already covered throughout the CNN module. The exact same shared feature map, already covered in Fast R-CNN, now serves both proposal generation and final classification.
This is a genuinely elegant reuse of the same computation for two genuinely different purposes, further extending the efficiency already covered as Fast R-CNN's own core improvement over R-CNN.
7. End-To-End Training

blocks.alt: RPN loss and detection loss combine for end to end training

blocks.text: A genuinely important training benefit connects back to joint training, already covered in Fast R-CNN. Faster R-CNN genuinely trains the entire pipeline end to end, region proposals included.
This extends the joint training already covered there even further, now encompassing the Region Proposal Network too, rather than leaving it as a genuinely separate, non-learned component.

blocks.text: 8. Completing The Speed Journey
This connects back to the speed problem, already covered in R-CNN. Faster R-CNN genuinely completes the speed journey started across all three R-CNN topics covered in this module.

From R-CNN's own genuinely severe slowness to a genuinely fast, fully integrated, end-to-end network, this progression, already covered across this module's first three topics, illustrates a genuinely clear, deliberate evolution.
9. Recognizing Why Faster R-CNN Is Genuinely Still A Strong Choice

blocks.alt: Needing high accuracy detection points toward using Faster R-CNN

blocks.text: This connects back to needing genuinely high detection accuracy. Its fully learned, integrated pipeline, already covered in this topic, tends to achieve genuinely strong accuracy.

This connects forward to YOLO and SSD, covered next in this module, favoring genuinely more speed. Faster R-CNN, already covered, often remains genuinely preferred when accuracy matters more than raw speed.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates Faster R-CNN's own conceptual anchor box mechanism, generating several anchor boxes at different scales for a single position, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
anchor_scales = [64, 128, 256]  # already covered as different sizes in the anchor box concept
anchor_ratios = [0.5, 1.0, 2.0]  # different aspect ratios, already covered in this topic

def generate_anchors(center_x, center_y, scales, ratios):
    # already covered as predefined anchor boxes in this topic
    anchors = []
    for scale in scales:
        for ratio in ratios:
            width = scale * (ratio ** 0.5)
            height = scale / (ratio ** 0.5)
            anchors.append((
                center_x - width / 2, center_y - height / 2,
                center_x + width / 2, center_y + height / 2,
            ))
    return anchors

anchors = generate_anchors(112, 112, anchor_scales, anchor_ratios)
print(f"Generated {len(anchors)} anchor boxes at a single position (already covered as the anchor box concept in this topic):")
for i, box in enumerate(anchors):
    print(f"  Anchor {i + 1}: {tuple(round(v, 1) for v in box)}")

print("\nThe Region Proposal Network, already covered in this topic, adjusts each of these anchors slightly to fit nearby objects")

blocks.text: 11. Object Detection Models: Progress Recap

items: Faster R-CNN replaces the separate region proposal algorithm with a learned Region Proposal Network.
The Region Proposal Network generates proposals directly from the same shared feature map.
Region proposals, classification, and box regression now all happen within one unified network.
It uses predefined anchor boxes of different sizes and shapes as starting points.
The same shared feature map now serves both proposal generation and final classification.
The entire pipeline, including region proposals, trains end to end.
This completes the speed journey from R-CNN's severe slowness to a fully integrated network.
It remains a strong choice when detection accuracy matters more than raw speed.
Next up: YOLO, an architecture that takes a fundamentally different, single-pass approach to detection.
